fasti.note: Caracalla (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus) marries Plautilla, daughter of the praetorian prefect Plautianus. Severan family returns to Africa (202-203); Lepcis Magna rebuilt.
The Geta of this year is the emperor's brother. Arch of Septimius Severus in the Forum dedicated. Martyrdom of Perpetua and Felicitas at Carthage (7 March).
Ludi Saeculares (Severan computation; inscription of the Acta).
Plautianus killed in the palace (22 January). Papinian praetorian prefect.

consuls: Marcus Nummius Umbrius Primus Senecio Albinus
fasti.note: Bandit Bulla Felix active in Italy (206-207).
Severus and his sons go to Britain for the Caledonian campaigns (208-211).
Geta made Augustus (209 or 210).
Severus dies at Eboracum (4 February), advising his sons to enrich the soldiers. Caracalla murders Geta in their mother's arms (26 December 211); damnatio memoriae; Papinian executed.
Constitutio Antoniniana extends citizenship to almost all free inhabitants (P. Giss. 40; dated 212). Asper and his son as joint consuls.
Caracalla's campaign against the Alamanni, their first appearance in the sources. Balbinus the future emperor (238).
Antoninianus (double denarius) introduced (215).
Massacre of the youth of Alexandria by Caracalla.
Baths of Caracalla dedicated (216). Parthian campaign.
Caracalla murdered near Carrhae (8 April); Macrinus, praetorian prefect, proclaimed, the first equestrian emperor. Battle of Nisibis; peace bought from Artabanus V for 200 million sesterces.
Elagabalus proclaimed at Raphanaea (16 May); Macrinus defeated near Antioch (8 June) and killed. Elagabalus took over Macrinus' consulship.
Elagabalus arrives in Rome with the sacred stone of Elagabal of Emesa.
Comazon, former actor and praetorian prefect, consul; Elagabalus marries the Vestal Aquilia Severa.
Severus Alexander adopted as Caesar.
Elagabalus and his mother Julia Soaemias killed by the praetorians (11 or 13 March); Severus Alexander accedes under Julia Maesa and Julia Mamaea. Ulpian praetorian prefect.

consuls: Lucius Roscius Aelianus Paculus Salvius Julianus
fasti.note: Marius Maximus, the biographer of the emperors. Ulpian killed by praetorians (223 or 228).
Ardashir defeats Artabanus IV at Hormozgan (28 April 224): end of the Arsacids, rise of the Sasanians.
Aqua Alexandrina built.
Cassius Dio the historian holds his second consulship with the emperor, then retires to Bithynia because the praetorians threatened him.
Ardashir invades Mesopotamia.
Severus Alexander's Persian expedition (231-233).
Dura-Europos synagogue paintings dated 244/245; house-church c. 232.
Pupienus the future emperor (238). Alamanni cross the Rhine.
Severus Alexander and Mamaea killed by soldiers near Mogontiacum (March); Maximinus Thrax proclaimed. Beginning of the 'crisis of the third century' (235-284).
Maximinus campaigns in Germany (Harzhorn battlefield, Lower Saxony, discovered 2008, dated c. 235-236).

Year of the Six Emperors: Gordian I and II proclaimed in Africa (January-March), killed at Carthage; the Senate's Pupienus and Balbinus; Maximinus killed at Aquileia; Pupienus and Balbinus murdered by praetorians; Gordian III sole emperor. Goths and Carpi sack Histria.
Revolt of Sabinianus in Africa; Legio III Augusta disbanded for its part in 238. Shapur I co-ruler; Hatra falls to the Persians (240/241). Mani begins preaching.
Timesitheus praetorian prefect; Gordian marries his daughter Tranquillina.
Gordian's Persian expedition; temple of Janus opened. Fuller nomenclature omitted where uncertain; third-century ordinarii are often known only from dating formulae (cognomina).
Battle of Rhesaina: Romans defeat Shapur. Timesitheus dies.
Gordian III dies after the battle of Misiche (Persian version, Res Gestae Divi Saporis) or murdered at Zaitha (Roman version); Philip the Arab makes peace for 500,000 aurei.
Philip campaigns against the Carpi.
Philip's son made Augustus.
Millennium of Rome celebrated (21 April 248) with secular games. Revolts of Pacatianus on the Danube and Iotapianus in the East.
Decius proclaimed by the Danubian army; Philip killed near Verona (September). Goths under Cniva invade.
Decius' edict requiring universal sacrifice; libelli from Egypt survive. Pope Fabian martyred (20 January). 'Plague of Cyprian' (c. 249-262).
Battle of Abritus (June/July): Decius and Herennius killed by Cniva's Goths, the first emperor to fall to a foreign enemy. Trebonianus Gallus accedes.
Shapur I takes Armenia; defeats a Roman army at Barbalissos (252 or 253).
Aemilian proclaimed in Moesia; Gallus and Volusianus killed at Interamna; Aemilian killed at Spoletium; Valerian accedes with his son Gallienus. Antioch sacked by Shapur (253 or 256).
Dura-Europos falls to the Persians (256/257), with siege mines and gas warfare evidenced archaeologically. Frankish and Alamannic raids.
Valerian's first edict against Christians.
Second edict: Cyprian of Carthage (14 September) and Pope Sixtus II executed.

Fuller nomenclature omitted where uncertain; third-century ordinarii are often known only from dating formulae (cognomina). Juthungi invade Italy; defeated near Augsburg (Augsburg victory altar, 260).
Valerian captured by Shapur I near Edessa; Gallienus sole emperor, ends the persecution. Postumus founds the Gallic Empire; Macrianus and Quietus in the East; Ingenuus and Regalianus on the Danube.
Odaenathus of Palmyra crushes the Macriani and Quietus. Postumus' consuls in the Gallic Empire run separately (260-274).
Odaenathus invades Persia, reaches Ctesiphon. Temple of Artemis at Ephesus burned by Goths.
Heruli sack Athens (267/268), repelled by Dexippus. Odaenathus murdered; Zenobia rules for Vaballathus.
Gallienus killed at the siege of Milan (September); Claudius II accedes; Goths defeated at Naissus (268 or 269).
Victory over the Goths at Naissus earns Claudius the title Gothicus. Postumus killed; Victorinus in Gaul. Zenobia's forces occupy Egypt (270).
Claudius dies of plague at Sirmium; Quintillus briefly; Aurelian accedes. Antoninianus silver content falls to around 2-5%.

Juthungi and Alamanni invade Italy; Roman defeat at Placentia, victories at Fanum Fortunae and Ticinum. Aurelian begins the walls of Rome (19 km, completed under Probus). Riot of the mint workers. Dacia evacuated (c. 271-275).
Aurelian defeats Zenobia at Immae and Emesa; Palmyra taken; Zenobia captured. Death of Shapur I (270 or 272).
Palmyra revolts again and is sacked. Firmus in Egypt. Tacitus the future emperor.
Tetricus surrenders at Châlons: Gallic Empire reabsorbed. Aurelian's triumph; coinage reform (aurelianianus marked XXI); temple of Sol Invictus dedicated (25 December); pork added to the dole.
Aurelian murdered at Caenophrurium in Thrace (autumn); an interregnum; Tacitus chosen.
Tacitus dies at Tyana; Florianus briefly; Probus accedes. Major Frankish and Alamannic invasion of Gaul (275-276).
Probus restores the Rhine frontier; resettles Bastarnae and others in Thrace.
Usurpations of Proculus and Bonosus at Cologne; Saturninus in the East.
Probus murdered at Sirmium by soldiers set to drain marshes; Carus accedes and makes his sons Carinus and Numerian Caesars.
Carus takes Ctesiphon and dies there (struck by lightning, per the sources).

Numerian found dead in his litter near Nicomedia; Diocletian proclaimed (20 November) and kills the prefect Aper; takes the consulship with Bassus. Era of Diocletian (Era of the Martyrs) counted from 29 August 284.
Diocletian's party dated by Diocletian II and Aristobulus. Carinus defeated or murdered at the Margus (spring); Diocletian sole emperor; Maximian made Caesar (July).
Maximian made Augustus (1 April 286 or 285). Carausius seizes Britain and northern Gaul (286 or 287).
Diocletian takes the name Jovius, Maximian Herculius.
Maximian's naval expedition against Carausius fails.
The Cassius Dio of this year is not the historian.
Both were praetorian prefects.
Tetrarchy: Constantius and Galerius made Caesars (1 March). Constantius takes Boulogne; Carausius murdered by Allectus.
Coinage reform: new silver argenteus, bronze nummus (c. 294-296).
Edict on marriage (incest) of Diocletian. Caesarean rescript on Manichaeans perhaps 302.
Constantius and Asclepiodotus recover Britain (Allectus killed); Arras medallion. Galerius defeated by Narseh near Carrhae (296/297). Egypt's revolt of Domitius Domitianus (297-298).

Galerius defeats Narseh in Armenia and captures his harem. Provincial reform: provinces roughly doubled and grouped into dioceses (c. 297; Verona List c. 303-314). Census-based tax system (iugatio and capitatio).
Peace of Nisibis: five Transtigritane regions ceded to Rome. Siege of Alexandria (297-298).
Purge of Christians from the army begins (c. 299).
Edict on Maximum Prices (late 301) and currency edict of Aphrodisias (1 September 301) retariffing the coinage.
Edict against the Manichaeans (302 or 297).
Great Persecution: first edict (23/24 February) orders churches destroyed and scriptures burned; further edicts 303-304. Vicennalia celebrated in Rome (20 November).
Fourth edict orders universal sacrifice.
Abdication of Diocletian at Nicomedia and Maximian at Milan (1 May); Constantius and Galerius Augusti, Severus and Maximinus Daia Caesars. Diocletian retires to Spalatum.
Constantius dies at Eboracum (25 July); his army proclaims Constantine. Maxentius proclaimed at Rome (28 October).

The fasti split. In Maximian's and Constantine's realm and at Rome, Maximian IX and Constantine; in Galerius' realm Severus II and Maximinus Caesar were proclaimed (Severus was captured and killed by Maxentius), after which the East used other formulae. Constantine marries Fausta.

Diocletian X and Galerius VII in the East (and briefly in Constantine's territory); in Maxentius' Rome, post-consular dating until April, then Maxentius and his son Romulus. Conference of Carnuntum (November): Licinius made Augustus.
Licinius and Constantine in the territories of Galerius and Constantine; Maxentius II and Romulus II in Italy and Africa. Romulus dies (309).
Andronicus and Probus in the East; Maxentius III alone in Italy. Maximian's revolt and death at Massilia.

In the East Galerius VIII and Maximinus II. Maxentius' territory used post-consular dating and then consuls of his own whose names are disputed. Galerius' edict of toleration (30 April) shortly before his death.
Maxentius IV in Rome until his death at the Milvian Bridge (28 October). Constantine's vision (Lactantius: the chi-rho on shields; Eusebius: the sign in the sky).

Maximinus Daia used Maximinus III in his territory until his defeat by Licinius at Campus Ergenus (30 April) and death at Tarsus. Licinius' letter on toleration (the 'Edict of Milan', June 313). Donatist schism; Council of Rome.
Council of Arles. First war between Constantine and Licinius (Cibalae, 316 or 314).
Arch of Constantine dedicated (decennalia).
Battle of Cibalae (8 October 316 by the now preferred date) and Campus Ardiensis; Licinius cedes the Balkans except Thrace.
Crispus, Constantine II and Licinius II made Caesars (1 March).
Arius' teaching controversial in Alexandria (c. 318).
Licinius' territory appears to have used different formulae from about this time.
Constantine's consuls; Licinius' realm probably used Licinius VI and his son. From 321 to 324 the two halves did not recognise each other's consuls.
Western consuls; the East under Licinius used post-consular or its own dating. Sunday made a legal day of rest (7 March 321).
Western consuls (not recognised by Licinius). Constantine defeats the Sarmatians.
Western consuls (not recognised by Licinius). Constantine's Gothic campaign crosses into Licinius' territory.
Constantine defeats Licinius at Adrianople (3 July) and Chrysopolis (18 September); sole emperor. Constantinople founded (8 November). Constantius made Caesar.

Proculus was removed during the year (his name erased from some inscriptions) and replaced by Julius Julianus. Council of Nicaea (May-July): Arius condemned; homoousios creed; date of Easter. Licinius executed.
Constantine's vicennalia in Rome; execution of Crispus at Pola and then of Fausta. Helena's pilgrimage to Palestine; churches of the Holy Sepulchre and Nativity.
The Constantius of this year is a praetorian prefect, not the emperor's son.
Bridge over the Danube at Oescus. Athanasius bishop of Alexandria.
Dedication of Constantinople (11 May).
Temple treasures confiscated; gold solidus spreads with the proceeds.
Constantine II defeats the Goths (20 April); treaty with the Tervingi. Law tying coloni to the land (CTh 5.17.1).
Constans made Caesar (25 December). Bordeaux Pilgrim's itinerary.

consuls: Amnius Manius Caesonius Nicomachus Anicius Paulinus
fasti.note: Sarmatians resettled within the empire (300,000 per the Origo).
Dalmatius made Caesar. Council of Tyre deposes Athanasius; exiled to Trier. Church of the Holy Sepulchre dedicated.
Tricennalia; death of Arius.
Constantine baptised by Eusebius of Nicomedia; dies near Nicomedia (22 May). Massacre of collateral relatives; his three sons Augusti (9 September).
Shapur II besieges Nisibis (337/338, 346, 350).
Constantine II killed invading Constans' territory near Aquileia.
Dedication Council of Antioch. Ulfila consecrated bishop of the Goths. Law against pagan sacrifice (CTh 16.10.2).
Council of Serdica splits East and West. Constans visits Britain in winter (342/343).
The West initially named Bonosus as colleague of Leontius before Sallustius replaced him.
Second siege of Nisibis.
Battle of Singara (348 or 344). Rome celebrates its 1,100th year; FEL TEMP REPARATIO coinage.
Magnentius usurps at Autun (18 January); Constans killed. Vetranio in Illyricum; Nepotianus at Rome (June).

Constantius' territory used post-consular dating (post consulatum Sergii et Nigriniani); Magnentius named himself and Gaiso. Gallus made Caesar (15 March). Battle of Mursa (28 September), one of the bloodiest of the century.
Magnentius' consuls in his remaining territory.
Magnentius defeated at Mons Seleucus; suicide at Lugdunum (10 August).
Gallus executed at Pola. Chronograph of 354 (Filocalus).

consuls: Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius
fasti.note: Silvanus' usurpation at Cologne (August), suppressed in 28 days. Julian made Caesar (6 November).
Constantius orders the temples closed (CTh 16.10.4).
Constantius' visit to Rome (April-May); obelisk erected in the Circus Maximus; removal of the Altar of Victory. Julian defeats the Alamanni at Strasbourg (August).
Earthquake destroys Nicomedia (24 August).
Councils of Ariminum and Seleucia; homoian creed. Shapur II takes Amida after a 73-day siege (Ammianus 19.1-8).
Julian proclaimed Augustus by his troops at Paris (February/March). Singara and Bezabde fall.
Constantius dies at Mopsucrenae (3 November) en route to fight Julian. Both consuls fled from Julian.
Mamertinus' panegyric on Julian. Julian's school law (17 June) bars Christians from teaching classics; attempt to rebuild the Jerusalem Temple (363). Fire in the temple of Apollo at Daphne.
Julian's Persian expedition; killed in a skirmish near Maranga (26 June). Jovian surrenders Nisibis, Singara and the Transtigritane regions.
Varronianus was Jovian's infant son. Jovian dies at Dadastana (17 February); Valentinian I proclaimed (26 February), makes Valens co-emperor (28 March); division of the army and court at Naissus.
Usurpation of Procopius at Constantinople (28 September). Tsunami in the eastern Mediterranean (21 July).
Gratian was aged seven. Procopius defeated at Thyatira and Nacolia, executed. Damasus bishop of Rome after riots (137 dead in a basilica, Ammianus 27.3).
Gratian made Augustus. 'Barbarian conspiracy' in Britain. Valens' first Gothic war (367-369).
Theodosius the Elder restores Britain (368-369).
Valentinianus Galates was Valens' infant son. Treaty with Athanaric on a boat in the Danube.
Trials for magic and adultery at Rome under Maximinus (369-371).
Treason and magic trials at Antioch (371-372).
Revolt of Firmus in Mauretania (372-375).
Death of Athanasius.
Ambrose made bishop of Milan. Quadi invade Pannonia.

No consuls: post-consular dating (post consulatum Gratiani III et Equitii). Valentinian I dies of a stroke at Brigetio while berating Quadi envoys (17 November); Valentinian II (aged four) proclaimed. Huns attack the Greuthungi.
Valens admits the Tervingi under Fritigern across the Danube. Theodosius the Elder executed at Carthage.
Battle ad Salices, indecisive.
Gratian defeats the Lentienses at Argentaria. Battle of Adrianople (9 August): Valens and two-thirds of the eastern field army killed.
Theodosius made Augustus at Sirmium (19 January). Ausonius' Gratiarum actio for his consulship.
Edict Cunctos populos (Thessalonica, 28 February) defines orthodoxy as the faith of Damasus and Peter of Alexandria.
Council of Constantinople. Athanaric received at Constantinople, dies there.
Treaty with the Goths (3 October): settlement in Thrace as federates under their own leaders. Gratian removes the Altar of Victory and cuts state funds for the pagan cults.
Magnus Maximus proclaimed in Britain; Gratian killed at Lugdunum (25 August). Arcadius made Augustus (19 January).
Symmachus' Relatio III on the Altar of Victory, answered by Ambrose.
Priscillian executed at Trier, the first heretic executed by Christian authority. Augustine's panegyric on Bauto at Milan.
Honorius was aged two (nobilissimus puer). Ambrose resists the court over a basilica for the Arians. Augustine's conversion at Milan.
Riot of the statues at Antioch. Maximus invades Italy; Valentinian II flees to Theodosius. Partition of Armenia with Persia (c. 387).
Magnus Maximus held a consulship of his own in his territory. Maximus defeated at Siscia and Poetovio, executed at Aquileia (28 August).
Theodosius' entry into Rome; Pacatus' panegyric.
Massacre at Thessalonica (some 7,000 killed); Theodosius' penance before Ambrose. Obelisk of Theodosius erected in the Hippodrome.
Theodosian laws banning sacrifice and temple visits (24 February, 16 June). Serapeum of Alexandria destroyed.
Valentinian II found hanged at Vienne (15 May); Arbogast proclaims Eugenius (22 August). Comprehensive ban on pagan cult (CTh 16.10.12, 8 November).
Eugenius, not recognised in the East, was sole consul in his territory. Honorius made Augustus (23 January). Last ancient Olympic Games traditionally dated to 393.
Nicomachus Flavianus named by Eugenius in the West until the Frigidus (5-6 September); Arbogast and Flavianus commit suicide.

The two young sons of Petronius Probus; Claudian's first Latin panegyric. Theodosius dies at Milan (17 January); empire divided between Arcadius (East) and Honorius (West) with Stilicho as guardian. Alaric's Goths revolt; Rufinus murdered (27 November). Huns raid Asia Minor and Syria through the Caucasus.
Alaric ravages Greece; Stilicho's expedition (397) ends inconclusively.

Caesarius nominated in the East, Atticus in the West, the regular pattern after 395. Revolt of Gildo in Africa; he transfers allegiance to Constantinople. Stilicho declared a public enemy by the eastern Senate.
Gildo defeated by his brother Mascezel. Honorius marries Stilicho's daughter Maria. Alaric made magister militum per Illyricum by the East.
Eutropius, the eunuch chamberlain, was the first eunuch consul; the West never recognised him, and he fell in August after Tribigild's revolt (damnatio memoriae). Claudian's In Eutropium.
Gainas' coup at Constantinople; Gothic troops massacred (12 July). Gainas killed by the Hun Uldin.
